findings.title: FromContext never reads the context-bound logger, so Plugin Request Completed logs lose pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname
findings.body: The new `FromContext` implementation calls the method `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` on the infra `*log.ConcreteLogger`. That method only derives a logger with the `traceID` from the trace span in the context; it does not return the logger that `log.WithContextualAttributes(ctx, p)` stores in the context. The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (contextual_logger_middleware.go) attaches the pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname attributes to a context-bound logger via `log.WithContextualAttributes`, and `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` to pick those attributes up (the explicit log params were removed from logger_middleware.go). Because the wrapper never retrieves the context-bound logger — it should call the package-level `log.FromContext(ctx)` — the "Plugin Request Completed" log line silently loses the pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname fields that were logged before this change whenever backend request logging (`PluginLogBackendRequests`) is enabled.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a discarded instance, breaking log assertions
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of `f`. Any code under test that logs through `FromContext` — which the updated `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now does — will record calls on a throwaway logger instance, so tests that inject a `TestLogger` and then assert on its `InfoLogs`/`ErrorLogs`/etc. will see zero calls and no captured messages. The fake should return `f` (or record on the shared instance) so log output through `FromContext` is observable in tests.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware added without any test coverage
findings.body: This PR introduces a new middleware that moves the `instrumentContext` logic (which endpoint/datasource/user attributes get attached and under which conditions, e.g. nil `DataSourceInstanceSettings` or nil `User`) out of the old instrumentation middleware, but adds no test for it. The only test touched is the renamed metrics middleware test, which covers metrics collection, not the contextual attributes. A regression in which attributes are attached — or in the interaction with `LoggerMiddleware.FromContext` — would go unnoticed.

findings.title: FromContext doc comment is a copy-paste of the New comment and misdescribes the method
findings.body: The doc comment for the new `FromContext` interface method reads "FromContext returns a new contextual Logger that has this logger's context plus the given context.", which is a verbatim copy of the `New` method's comment. `FromContext` takes a `context.Context` and (per its implementations) extracts/derives a logger from it — it does not merge variadic key/value pairs into the logger's context. The comment misleads implementers and callers about the method's contract.
